newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai PM cautions against wrong economic signals.
newsitem.headline: Thai PM cautions against wrong economic signals.

text.p: Thailand should not send wrong economic signals to convince foreign investors it is serious in tackling its economic problems, Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchiayudh said on Wednesday.
Investors should be made aware that the government would not spend lavishly when the Thai economy faced a slowdown and would not push for faster economic growth, he told reporters.

"If we show that we don't care about economic stability, we don't tighten belts or move to boost exports, but still seek to push for fast economic growth of eight or 10 percent, that would be wrong signals that could provoke more baht attacks," he said.

Chavalit was referring to the heavy selling pressure against the baht in foreign exchange markets over the past two weeks that led the Bank of Thailand to keep local interest rates high to squeeze funds available for currency speculation.
On Tuesday, the government announced a six-percent budget cut this year and said state enterprises would defer investments totalling up to 62 billion baht ($2.38 billion) in 1997.
The Thai economy expanded 6.7 percent in 1996, its lowest rate of growth in 10 years.
